claims.text: Labels are key/value pairs under metadata.labels; many objects can carry the same label, while a name is unique among objects of one kind in a namespace (a Pod's name among the Pods of its namespace).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Working with Objects > Labels and Selectors; Object Names and IDs

claims.text: kubectl get with -l <selector> lists only objects whose labels match the selector; the match is on labels, not on object names.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Labels and Selectors (Using label selectors with kubectl / LIST and WATCH filtering)

claims.text: In an equality-based selector, comma-separated requirements are ANDed: an object must satisfy all of them (app=web,track=stable).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Labels and Selectors (Label selectors: comma separator acts as logical AND)

claims.text: Kubernetes attaches no meaning to user-chosen label keys like app or track; labels do not directly imply semantics to the core system and only matter to objects that select on them.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Labels and Selectors ('Labels do not provide uniqueness'; 'do not directly imply semantics to the core system')

claims.text: kubectl get --show-labels adds a LABELS column listing each object's labels as key=value pairs joined by commas.
deploy/k8s/lessons/labelled-pods.yaml@stage-2 declares three caddy:2.10.0 Pods in donhang: web-stable (app=web, track=stable), web-test (app=web, track=test), proxy (app=proxy, track=stable).

scripts/k8s/labels.sh@stage-2 applies namespace.yaml, deletes then applies labelled-pods.yaml, waits Ready, lists with --show-labels and three selectors (lines 8-25), then deletes the three Pods (lines 27-28); output as in outputs/stage-2/scripts/k8s/labels.txt.
When no object matches, kubectl get pods -n donhang -l <selector> prints 'No resources found in donhang namespace.'
claims.source_hint: executed kubectl v1.34.3: kubectl get pods -n donhang -l app=proxy,track=test

claims.text: A label change such as track: test does not change how the Pod's container runs; it only changes which selectors match the Pod.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Labels and Selectors (labels are identifying metadata)
